text: Noology [Gr. nouV , reason, + logoV , theory]: Ger. Noologie ; Fr. noologie ; Ital. noologia (the equivalents are suggested). That part of philosophy which deals with intuitive truths of reason; as distinct from Dianoiology, which deals with truths discursively or demonstratively established. A term suggested by Sir William Hamilton, Reid's Works , note A, § v, but having no currency. Hamilton probably derived it from Kant ( Krit . d . reinen Vernunft , 643). It is used by Crusius for psychology. ( J.D. )
